title: Inspect and extend: Compose browse, tabs, and settings views
objective: Use the real implementation in `Sources/ContentView.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve observable store injection, navigation, toolbar actions, and settings binding.
problem: A view tree is a set of nested controls that observe one shared store. Trace the store environment from ContentView into controls and see how a setting changes the core behavior. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Sources/ContentView.swift` and the related project files: Sources/ContentView.swift; Sources/Screens/BrowseView.swift; Sources/Screens/SettingsView.swift.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to observable store injection, navigation, toolbar actions, and settings binding.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: The views demonstrate a subset of a browser workflow and are not a production browser UX.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A view tree is a set of nested controls that observe one shared store. Trace the store environment from ContentView into controls and see how a setting changes the core behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Sources/ContentView.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
